title: Statement import resurrects a row the person deleted: decide tombstone behaviour (bank sync skips, /bulk re-adds)
description:
Found by the import-idempotency audit (budget-9ekv), documented in docs/evidence/import-idempotency/REPORT.md.

Scenario: POST /transactions/bulk a statement, delete one imported row in the register (soft delete), import the same file again -> the deleted row is inserted again as a new row.

Why: both dedupe readers (findImportIdsLike / findImportRowTexts in api/src/budget/store/transactions.ts) filter NOT deleted, and the unique index transactions_account_import_id_uq is WHERE import_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT deleted, so the tombstone is invisible to the import.

Asymmetry: bank sync already skips a row it has shadowed even when deleted (api/src/connections/sync.ts + sync-idempotent.test.ts 'a transaction the user deleted comes back upstream: skipped, stays deleted').

Decision needed (owner): should a re-import of the same file resurrect a row the person deleted? Two options:
(a) tombstone-aware statement import: make the dedupe queries also read deleted rows for the dedupe decision (keep the unique index as is), so a re-import counts the row as a duplicate; matches bank sync.
(b) keep today's behaviour and document it as intended: deleting a row means 'import it fresh next time'.
No migration needed either way; (a) is a small change in the dedupe reads plus a test in api/src/budget/routes/transactions.test.ts. Do not change behaviour before the decision.
